title: Pairing and Collaborative Review Session
summary: Master Pairing and Collaborative Review Session through explanation, prediction, implementation, and review.

challenges.title: Recall checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Without reopening the lesson, explain Pairing and Collaborative Review Session in your own words. Include the problem it solves, the core mechanism, and one boundary or failure.
challenges.hint: Use “Roles” as a cue, then close the lesson again.

challenges.title: Prediction checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Choose one example or source file from this mission. Predict its behavior for a normal input and a changed or invalid input before running or revealing the reference. Explain the rule separating the outcomes.
challenges.hint: Change one condition at a time so the result teaches a rule.

challenges.title: Build and prove checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Implement, debug, or adapt the mission exercise yourself. Record the acceptance criterion, command or interaction used to verify it, failure evidence, and one tradeoff. Do not paste the reference solution.
challenges.hint: A passing check, measured result, focused diff, or reproducible demo is stronger than ‘done.’

# Pairing and Collaborative Review Session

## Roles

| Interval | Driver | Navigator | Reviewer/operator |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–25 minutes | | | |
| 25–50 minutes | | | |
| 50–75 minutes | | | |

The driver controls the editor and narrates. The navigator asks predictive and
system-level questions. The reviewer checks requirements, risks, and evidence.
Rotate roles even when one person has more experience.

## Shared prediction

What should happen before the code or check runs?


What is the most likely failure or counterexample?


## Review prompts

- Which requirement does this change satisfy?
- What assumption is not represented by a test?
- Where can invalid state enter?
- What happens on retry, concurrency, partial failure, or unauthorized access?
- Is this feedback blocking correctness or suggesting a preference?
- What operational signal would reveal failure?

## Individual reconstruction

After the shared session, each person independently writes:

- the core mechanism;
- one tradeoff;
- one failure case;
- how to reproduce or verify the result;
- the next code change they could make alone.

If one person cannot do this, schedule a solo reconstruction before advancing.
